minutes.headline: Planning Board approved two ANR plans, continued the 101 Pleasant St subdivision hearing to May 10, and chose an RFP for the master plan.
minutes.summary: The board approved two ANR plans and a de minimis change at Tri-Town Landing. It heard a long review of a six-duplex subdivision at 101 Pleasant Street and continued it to May 10. It asked BrightFarms for a full site plan modification, favored an RFP over a direct MRPC contract for the master plan, and agreed to send a letter to an absent member.

public_comment.topic: Asked about the affordable housing component and runoff into a neighbor's pond. Raised the applicant's history with the town and urged bonds.
A neighbor at 182 Mass Ave agreed with the comment on the applicant's character and said a bridge was built illegally in the woods.

public_comment.stated_role: representing her mother at 39 Pleasant Street
public_comment.topic: Called it an aggressive proposal on a wetland-encumbered site. Said comments are coming and asked about the affordable unit ownership model and private road maintenance.
Corrected the conservation commission continuation date to the 19th.
Asked about the road cut moratorium and whether the abutter's permission is needed for the road entrance overlapping her driveway.

votes.motion: Approve the ANR plan for 111 Memphis Road as presented
Approve the ANR plan for 360 Flat Hill Road
Accept the de minimis change for Tri-Town Landing
Continue the North End Subaru hearing to May 10
Continue the 101 Pleasant Street hearing to May 10

budget_items.what_was_said: The planner described how a covenant or financial security for roadway and utility work is held and released, with an inflation contingency in a third-party account.
The board preferred an RFP to a direct MRPC scope of services, which it found not detailed enough.

decisions.decision: Add an ANR and wetlands workshop to the May 24 agenda and seek legal guidance from town counsel.
The applicant will submit written waiver requests with compelling reasons, to be heard May 10.
The planner will ask town counsel, in writing, whether the board can condition private road ownership or require a different stormwater design.
BrightFarms will be told to file a full site plan modification, not a de minimis change.
The planner will draft a master plan RFP for the board in early May.
The planner will draft a letter to the absent member for board review at the next meeting.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board continued the hearing on a six-duplex subdivision at 101 Pleasant Street to May 10, after a long review that ran past an hour.
The board approved two ANR plans, 111 Memphis Road and 360 Flat Hill Road, each by a 3-0 vote.
The board told BrightFarms to file a full site plan modification rather than a de minimis change.
The board favored a request for proposals over a direct MRPC contract for the master plan consultant, and the planner will draft the RFP in early May.
The board accepted a de minimis change for Tri-Town Landing and continued the North End Subaru hearing to May 10, both 3-0.

why_it_matters: The 101 Pleasant Street subdivision is still undecided, and residents who live nearby or abut the site can still comment, since neighbors raised runoff, wetlands, private road maintenance and a driveway overlap.
Choosing an RFP means the master plan consultant will be picked through a competitive process, and that plan guides future zoning and development decisions in town.
watch_next: May 10 meeting: the continued hearings for 101 Pleasant Street and North End Subaru, plus the applicant's written waiver requests.
Town counsel's written answer on whether the board can condition private road ownership or require a different stormwater design, and the draft master plan RFP due in early May.
